messages.content: Erythema typically presents as localized redness caused by cutaneous vasodilation, often reflecting increased blood flow to the underlying dermis. During a physical exam, you should assess for the extent of the redness, warmth to the touch, potential tenderness or edema, and whether the area involves the mucous membranes. The intensity of the erythema can provide clues to the etiology, ranging from superficial sunburn-like reactions to signs of infection or acute inflammation.
